title: KV soft-tiering: TTL+LRU hybrid with prefix-aware safety and serializability sketch
creator: Sofia Ramos
description: Design and implement a 'soft-tier' eviction policy that combines TTL windows and LRU scoring with explicit prefix-awareness and a set of lightweight correctness guards. Goal: reduce pathological eviction cascades during continuous batching and prefetch while preserving strong observable guarantees (serializability of cache effects w.r.t. requests) and keeping tail-latency/regressions within performance SLOs.
background: We've observed scenarios where aggressive prefetching and continuous batching cause long-lived prefetched KV prefixes to displace hot per-request keys on GPUs, leading to repeated cold misses and latency spikes for customer requests. Existing TTL-only or pure-LRU strategies oscillate under heavy mix shifts. Several tickets touch related invariants (see dependencies) but none provide a simple hybrid with lightweight correctness checks suitable for dedicated GPU slab allocation.
proposed_solution: Introduce a two-tier scoring model: (1) soft-tier TTL band that gives newly prefetched sequences a short protected residency (configurable ms window) and (2) LRU ranks within each prefix group for longer-term eviction decisions. Add atomic prefix pin/unpin tokens for in-flight requests and an ordinal-based serialization token so that eviction that would remove a key currently referenced by an inflight request is disallowed; instead eviction must mark slot for reclamation after outstanding references drain. Implement a small correctness verifier that runs in parallel during integration tests to assert that no request observed a missing KV it should have seen given its logical order.
tradeoffs: - Pros: reduces repeated cache thrashing, keeps prefetched data useful for short bursty workloads, preserves per-request correctness.- Cons: adds metadata per slot (prefix id, refcount, ordinal) and slightly more complex eviction path; small memory overhead and more branches in hot path.- Operational: requires tuning TTL band per workload; misconfiguration could temporarily increase resident set and cold misses.
acceptance_criteria: Eviction policy implemented behind feature flag; default off
Integration tests with correctness verifier detect zero violations across 1M synthetic request traces
Latency p99 regression < 5% compared to baseline for mixed prefetch workload
Cache miss-rate for target workload decreases or stays flat vs. baseline within 10%
No request-level observable consistency violations in canary runs (see rollout)
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Spec and API - add slot metadata fields (prefix_id, soft_ttl_expiry, ordinal, refcount) and a flag to enable soft-tier policy (2 days)
Phase 2: Eviction engine - implement hybrid evictor that consults soft-ttl band then prefix-LRU buckets; ensure atomic pin/unpin semantics using compare-and-swap on slot header (4 days)
Phase 3: Correctness verifier - lightweight serializability checker integrated into jittered integration harness (3 days)
Phase 4: Fuzz + perf - run eviction fuzzbench against representative batching traces and optimize hot path (4 days)
Phase 5: Docs and defaults - add runtime knobs to Console and default heuristics for common workloads (2 days)
testing_plan: Unit tests for slot header CAS and refcount transitions
Deterministic simulator: run 1M mixed traces (prefetch heavy, request heavy, churn) and assert verifier sees no ordering anomalies
Fuzzbench: integrate into existing kv-eviction-fuzzbench harness (PR #3456) and capture edge cases
Performance microbenchmarks: measure additional CPU cycles and GPU memory overhead per slot; target <1.5% overall throughput regression
Canary: roll out on 5% of dedicated pools for 48h with metrics alerting on cache-miss, p99 latency, and correctness verifier signals
rollout_plan: Enable feature-flagged binary in staging; run long-running smoke tests (24h)
Canary to 5% of Dedicated pools with read-only prefix prefetch workloads (48h)
If no violations and metrics within thresholds, increase to 25% and enable on a blended workload set (72h)
Full rollout gated on customer-impact alerts and SRE sign-off
metrics: p50/p95/p99 tail latency for text-generation workloads
risks: Increased resident set leading to higher GPU memory pressure under mis-tuned TTL
CAS contention on slot headers under extreme concurrency could add latency to hot path
Edge cases where prefix groups are large and prefix-LRU buckets become skewed
Operational complexity for non-engineering customers selecting TTL heuristics
next_steps: Pair with infra to instrument per-slot memory overhead metric
Prototype verifier in simulator and ship initial tests
Schedule design review with runtime and SRE on 2025-02-25
